sections.h2: Selling fast in Fond du Lac: your options
sections.html:
A Fond du Lac owner has three ways out: sign with a listing agent, line up a buyer without help, or take a cash bid. Cash gives you the firmest grip on the closing date. Your reason for moving and the state of the roof, kitchen and furnace will steer the choice.

  • Agent listing: works for a tidy house and a seller who can leave it open for tours through an ordinary marketing stretch.
  • Private sale: you pick the number, draft the terms and own every state form.
  • Cash offer: common when repairs were put off, a relative left you the house, tenants live there, or you need a guaranteed day.

Prices run modest, with a middle home value of $173,700. A large repair bill takes a bigger bite out of a price that size. Ask a contractor for a written quote, then set it beside what the finished work could add before you choose between renovating and selling untouched.

Fond du Lac is the county seat and its population has barely moved. Use these citywide figures as a loose frame when an offer arrives.

The median monthly cost for an owner with a mortgage is $1,351, and the average commute lasts 19.3 minutes. Roughly 86.4 percent of residents did not move in the past year, which suggests many of your likely buyers already live nearby.

Lake Winnebago ends at the city's edge, and two branches of the Fond du Lac River join within its limits. With that much water around, the Inspection Division enforces floodplain rules alongside zoning and property maintenance. Check whether your lot is in a flood area before you commit to a closing date.

The city has four historic districts: South Main Street, North Main Street, Linden Street, and East Division and Sheboygan Streets. An older house near one of them may face extra review, so ask Inspection Services before planning outside work.

sections.h2: Which repairs need a permit in Fond du Lac?
sections.html:
Most house work in Fond du Lac needs a permit, and the city has adopted the state building, mechanical, electrical and plumbing codes. The Building Inspections page covers new buildings, additions, interior and exterior alterations, siding, roofing, garages, decks, windows, pools, sheds, patios, fences, electrical work, water heater and furnace replacements, and plumbing.

Small alterations and maintenance may be waived by the building inspector. Call 920-322-3570 to ask if your job counts. The city also publishes packets for fences, decks, sheds, pools, ramps and garages that show what a finished project should include.

  • List projects from recent years and note which had permits.
  • Find out if any permit still needs a final inspection.
  • Collect receipts and contractor names for the roof, windows, siding and furnace.

The Housing and Code Enforcement page says municipal code reaches property maintenance and public nuisance issues. If a notice has come in for your house, resolve it or disclose it ahead of signing.

If the property has one to four dwelling units, you fill out the real estate condition report and deliver it within 10 days of an accepted offer. Chapter 709 reaches sales, exchanges and land contracts, leaving out transfers the state fee excuses.

"Aware" on the form means you have notice or knowledge of a condition. You may swap in a professional's written findings, from an engineer, surveyor, pest control operator or contractor, for your own answer on the matching line, as long as they come on time and tie plainly to that line. Hand it over late and the buyer can cancel in writing for two business days once the 10 days are up.

By its own terms the report is no warranty and no stand-in for inspections. Buyers will usually order one anyway, so keep your answers in line with what the city or your insurer already knows.

sections.h2: Recording the deed and the transfer fee
sections.html:
Take the deed to the Fond du Lac County Register of Deeds on the first floor at 160 S. Macy Street, where the usual recording fee is $30. The counter opens weekdays at 7:45 a.m. and closes at 4:30 p.m., holidays excepted, but real estate recording stops at 3:30 p.m. and late papers are handled the next business day. Call 920-929-3018 with questions.

Documents can be e-recorded, mailed or brought in. Its LandShark system searches and sells recorded documents back to 1839, and a free alert service called Land Notification tells owners when something is recorded under their name or parcel number.

Section 77.22 puts the transfer fee on the seller at 30 cents per $100 of value. The transfer return is filed electronically and signed by both sides. Call the county treasurer for what is owed on taxes, and the closing agent will split it.

sections.h2: Steps after you accept an offer
sections.html:
After you agree to terms, the chores run in a fixed order for a cash buyer or a borrower.

  • Hand over the condition report in the 10-day window.
  • Close out or disclose open permits and city notices.
  • Sign the deed, and have both sides sign the electronic transfer return.
  • Record the deed and pay the recording fee.
  • Take your mortgage payoff and tax share out of the proceeds.

Cash buyers need no appraisal or loan approval, so closing can land on the day you name. A listing brings showings, an inspection and a lender's clock into the mix. Whichever route you take, keep copies of every signed page, and write down the day each deadline began so no date slips past.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Fond du Lac house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer sets the price around the work needed. A property with one to four units still requires the condition report.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Fond du Lac County?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 per document. The seller separately pays the state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value.

faqs.q: What are the Register of Deeds hours in Fond du Lac County?
faqs.a: Weekdays, 7:45 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except holidays. Real estate recording runs 7:45 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., and later submissions go in the next business day.

faqs.q: Does a new roof or window job need a permit in Fond du Lac?
faqs.a: Both are on the city's list of permit work. The inspector may waive minor maintenance, so call 920-322-3570 first.

faqs.q: I inherited a Fond du Lac house but never lived there. What changes?
faqs.a: A court-appointed personal representative or trustee who never occupied the house skips the condition report, and transfers by will or descent owe no transfer fee. Ask the register of deeds how to record the paperwork.
